q: Molecular biology is the branch of biology that seeks to understand the ____ basis of biological activity in and between cells, including biomolecular synthesis, modification, mechanisms, and interactions.
e: Molecular biology is the branch of biology that seeks to understand the molecular basis of biological activity in and between cells, including biomolecular synthesis, modification, mechanisms, and interactions. Write molecular in the gap.

q: The study of chemical, physical structures, and functions of biological ____ is known as molecular biology.
e: The study of chemical, physical structures, and functions of biological macromolecules is known as molecular biology. That missing piece is macromolecules.

q: ____ acids are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell which direct the process of protein synthesis by determining the inherited characteristics of every living thing.
e: Nucleic acids are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell which direct the process of protein synthesis by determining the inherited characteristics of every living thing. That missing piece is Nucleic.

q: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ____ (RNA).
e: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA). Write ribonucleic acid in the gap.

q: DNA is the master blueprint for life and constitutes the ____ material in all free-living organisms and most viruses.
e: DNA is the master blueprint for life and constitutes the genetic material in all free-living organisms and most viruses. Write genetic in the gap.

q: RNA is the genetic material of certain viruses, but it is also found in all living cells, where it plays an important role in certain processes such as the making of ____.
e: RNA is the genetic material of certain viruses, but it is also found in all living cells, where it plays an important role in certain processes such as the making of proteins. The blank is proteins.

q: DNA is a ____ structure consisting of two polynucleotide strands twine around each other.
e: DNA is a double helix structure consisting of two polynucleotide strands twine around each other. The blank is double helix.

q: Each polynucleotide strand is made up of many ____ molecules.
e: Each polynucleotide strand is made up of many nucleotide molecules. That missing piece is nucleotide.

q: Each nucleotide in DNA is composed of a five-carbon ____ sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogen-containing base, all linked together by covalent bonds.
e: Each nucleotide in DNA is composed of a five-carbon deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogen-containing base, all linked together by covalent bonds. Write deoxyribose in the gap.

q: Four different nitrogenous bases in DNA that can be categorized into two different forms: purines and ____.
e: Four different nitrogenous bases in DNA that can be categorized into two different forms: purines and pyrimidines. That missing piece is pyrimidines.

q: The purine bases are adenine (A) and ____.
e: The purine bases are adenine (A) and guanine. Write guanine in the gap.

q: The purine bases have ____ fused rings in their chemical structures.
e: The purine bases have two fused rings in their chemical structures. The blank is two.

q: The pyrimidine bases are cytosine (C) and ____.
e: The pyrimidine bases are cytosine (C) and thymine. The blank is thymine.

q: The pyrimidine bases have a ____ ring in their chemical structure.
e: The pyrimidine bases have a single ring in their chemical structure. Write single in the gap.

q: Each strand forms a backbone of alternating ____ groups and sugars.
e: Each strand forms a backbone of alternating phosphate groups and sugars. Write phosphate in the gap.

q: The bases of each nucleotide are attached to each sugar and protrude ____ at regular intervals along each strand.
e: The bases of each nucleotide are attached to each sugar and protrude inward at regular intervals along each strand. The blank is inward.

q: There is a constant total distance between the ____ backbones.
e: There is a constant total distance between the sugar-phosphate backbones. The blank is sugar-phosphate.

q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are not identical but are, instead, ____ to each other.
e: The two strands of a DNA molecule are not identical but are, instead, complementary to each other. That missing piece is complementary.

q: This means that a purine molecule is always paired with a ____ molecule.
e: This means that a purine molecule is always paired with a pyrimidine molecule. That missing piece is pyrimidine.

q: Specifically, adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T) and guanine (G) always pairs with ____.
e: Specifically, adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T) and guanine (G) always pairs with cytosine. Write cytosine in the gap.

q: This specific pairing rule is called ____ base pairing.
e: This specific pairing rule is called complementary base pairing. The blank is complementary.

q: ____ bonds link each complementary base pair.
e: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary base pair. That missing piece is Hydrogen.

q: A and T are joined by ____ hydrogen bonds, while C and G with three hydrogen bonds.
e: A and T are joined by two hydrogen bonds, while C and G with three hydrogen bonds. The blank is two.

q: C and G are joined by ____ hydrogen bonds.
e: C and G are joined by three hydrogen bonds. The blank is three.

q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are ____, meaning they run in opposite directions.
e: The two strands of a DNA molecule are antiparallel, meaning they run in opposite directions. That missing piece is antiparallel.

q: One strand lies in 5' to 3' direction and another strand in ____ direction.
e: One strand lies in 5' to 3' direction and another strand in 3' to 5' direction. The blank is 3' to 5'.

q: The 5' and 3' come from the numbering of the carbons on the ____ sugar.
e: The 5' and 3' come from the numbering of the carbons on the deoxyribose sugar. That missing piece is deoxyribose.

q: The phosphate group is on the 5' carbon, and the OH group is on the ____ carbon.
e: The phosphate group is on the 5' carbon, and the OH group is on the 3' carbon. That missing piece is 3'.

q: Therefore, the end with phosphate group is always referred as 5' end and the opposite end of it will be ____ end.
e: Therefore, the end with phosphate group is always referred as 5' end and the opposite end of it will be 3' end. The blank is 3'.

q: By convention, the sequence of a DNA strand is always written in the ____ direction.
e: By convention, the sequence of a DNA strand is always written in the 5' to 3' direction. Write 5' to 3' in the gap.

q: Like DNA, RNA is a ____ of nucleotides.
e: Like DNA, RNA is a polymer of nucleotides. Write polymer in the gap.

q: RNA contains four nucleotides with the bases adenine (A), uracil (U), cytosine (C), and ____.
e: RNA contains four nucleotides with the bases adenine (A), uracil (U), cytosine (C), and guanine. That missing piece is guanine.

q: Unlike DNA, RNA is ____.
e: Unlike DNA, RNA is single-stranded. The blank is single-stranded.

q: However, tRNA can fold back on itself, and complementary base pairing within the same molecule stabilizes the ____ structure.
e: However, tRNA can fold back on itself, and complementary base pairing within the same molecule stabilizes the looped structure. The blank is looped.

q: Since all RNA molecules are produced from a DNA template, all are synthesized in the ____.
e: Since all RNA molecules are produced from a DNA template, all are synthesized in the nucleus. The blank is nucleus.

q: Messenger RNA (mRNA) acts as the template for ____.
e: Messenger RNA (mRNA) acts as the template for translation. The blank is translation.

q: Transfer RNA (tRNA) carries specific ____ to mRNA at ribosome.
e: Transfer RNA (tRNA) carries specific amino acid to mRNA at ribosome. The blank is amino acid.

q: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) reads the ____ on mRNA.
e: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) reads the codon on mRNA. Write codon in the gap.

q: DNA is the ____ material responsible for passing genetic information from cell to cell and generation to generation.
e: DNA is the hereditary material responsible for passing genetic information from cell to cell and generation to generation. That missing piece is hereditary.

q: In total, there are around ____ base pairs in the DNA of a typical mammalian cell.
e: In total, there are around 3.2 billion base pairs in the DNA of a typical mammalian cell. Write 3.2 billion in the gap.

q: The DNA molecule is a very ____ structure which normally passes from generation to generation without change.
e: The DNA molecule is a very stable structure which normally passes from generation to generation without change. The blank is stable.

q: Only rarely does DNA ____.
e: Only rarely does DNA mutate. Write mutate in the gap.

q: Its two separate strands are joined only with hydrogen bonds, which allow them to separate during DNA replication and ____ synthesis.
e: Its two separate strands are joined only with hydrogen bonds, which allow them to separate during DNA replication and protein synthesis. The blank is protein.

q: By having the base pairs within the helical structure of the deoxyribose-phosphate backbone, the genetic information is to some extent ____ from being corrupted by outside chemical and physical forces.
e: By having the base pairs within the helical structure of the deoxyribose-phosphate backbone, the genetic information is to some extent protected from being corrupted by outside chemical and physical forces. Write protected in the gap.

q: Base pairing leads to DNA being able to replicate and to transfer information to ____.
e: Base pairing leads to DNA being able to replicate and to transfer information to mRNA. The blank is mRNA.

q: The function of the remarkable molecule, DNA depends on the ____ of base pairs that it possesses.
e: The function of the remarkable molecule, DNA depends on the sequence of base pairs that it possesses. That missing piece is sequence.

q: DNA replication is the making of an ____ of the DNA molecule.
e: DNA replication is the making of an exact copy of the DNA molecule. That missing piece is exact copy.

q: The replication is made by a ____ method, which was predicted by Watson and Crick and proven by Meselson and Stahl.
e: The replication is made by a semiconservative method, which was predicted by Watson and Crick and proven by Meselson and Stahl. Write semiconservative in the gap.

q: It is regarded as semiconservative because each of the resulting two molecules consists of one old strand and one ____ strand.
e: It is regarded as semiconservative because each of the resulting two molecules consists of one old strand and one new strand. That missing piece is new.

q: Replication begins at special sites called ____ of replication, the replication bubbles form.
e: Replication begins at special sites called origins of replication, the replication bubbles form. The blank is origins.

q: ____ enzymes unwind the double helix and unzip the two parental strands by breaking hydrogen bonds.
e: Helicase enzymes unwind the double helix and unzip the two parental strands by breaking hydrogen bonds. The blank is Helicase.

q: The separated two parental strands act as ____.
e: The separated two parental strands act as templates. Write templates in the gap.

q: Single-stranded binding proteins act as scaffolding, holding the two strands ____.
e: Single-stranded binding proteins act as scaffolding, holding the two strands apart. That missing piece is apart.

q: ____ lessens the tension on the tight helix ahead of the replication fork.
e: Topoisomerase lessens the tension on the tight helix ahead of the replication fork. Write Topoisomerase in the gap.

q: At each end of the replication bubble is a replication ____, a Y-shaped region where the new strands of DNA are elongating.
e: At each end of the replication bubble is a replication fork, a Y-shaped region where the new strands of DNA are elongating. That missing piece is fork.

q: DNA polymerase III cannot ____ the synthesis of a new DNA strand.
e: DNA polymerase III cannot initiate the synthesis of a new DNA strand. Write initiate in the gap.

q: The preexisting chain actually consists of RNA primer produced by an enzyme called ____.
e: The preexisting chain actually consists of RNA primer produced by an enzyme called primase. The blank is primase.

q: DNA polymerase can only add complementary nucleotides to the free ____ end of the primer, never to the 5' end.
e: DNA polymerase can only add complementary nucleotides to the free 3' end of the primer, never to the 5' end. That missing piece is 3'.

q: Thus, a new DNA strand can elongate only in the ____ direction.
e: Thus, a new DNA strand can elongate only in the 5' to 3' direction. The blank is 5' to 3'.

q: Although it builds both new strands in the 5' to 3' direction, one strand is formed towards the replication fork in continuous and linear fashion, called the ____ strand.
e: Although it builds both new strands in the 5' to 3' direction, one strand is formed towards the replication fork in continuous and linear fashion, called the leading strand. The blank is leading.

q: The other strand, the lagging strand, forms in direction away from the replication fork, in a series of segments called ____ fragments.
e: The other strand, the lagging strand, forms in direction away from the replication fork, in a series of segments called okazaki fragments. Write okazaki in the gap.

q: Each Okazaki fragment is about ____ nucleotides long and then they are joined into one continuous strand by the enzyme DNA ligase.
e: Each Okazaki fragment is about 100-200 nucleotides long and then they are joined into one continuous strand by the enzyme DNA ligase. Write 100-200 in the gap.

q: DNA polymerase I carry out mismatch repair, a kind of ____ that corrects errors.
e: DNA polymerase I carry out mismatch repair, a kind of proofreading that corrects errors. Write proofreading in the gap.

q: Damaged regions of DNA are excised out by DNA ____.
e: Damaged regions of DNA are excised out by DNA nuclease. That missing piece is nuclease.

q: To protect against the possible loss of genes at the end of the chromosomes, eukaryotes have special nonsense nucleotide sequences (____) at the ends of chromosomes that repeat thousands of times.
e: To protect against the possible loss of genes at the end of the chromosomes, eukaryotes have special nonsense nucleotide sequences (TAAGGG) at the ends of chromosomes that repeat thousands of times. The blank is TAAGGG.

q: These protective ends are called ____, which are created and controlled by the enzyme telomerase.
e: These protective ends are called telomeres, which are created and controlled by the enzyme telomerase. Write telomeres in the gap.

q: Genetic code is a set of rules for determining how genetic information in the form of a nucleotide sequence is converted to an ____ sequence of a protein.
e: Genetic code is a set of rules for determining how genetic information in the form of a nucleotide sequence is converted to an amino acid sequence of a protein. That missing piece is amino acid.

q: Researchers knew that there are only four nucleotides in RNA, but ____ different kinds of amino acids.
e: Researchers knew that there are only four nucleotides in RNA, but 20 different kinds of amino acids. The blank is 20.

q: Thus, the minimum combination of the four nucleotides was a ____ code, which could produce 64 possible combinations.
e: Thus, the minimum combination of the four nucleotides was a triplet code, which could produce 64 possible combinations. Write triplet in the gap.

q: From this reasoning came the triplet hypothesis, which proposed that the genetic code consists of a combination of ____ nucleotides, called a codon.
e: From this reasoning came the triplet hypothesis, which proposed that the genetic code consists of a combination of three nucleotides, called a codon. The blank is three.

q: AUG is a ____ codon.
e: AUG is a start codon. The blank is start.

q: AUG also codes for the amino acid ____.
e: AUG also codes for the amino acid methionine. Write methionine in the gap.

q: UAA, UAG, and UGA are ____ codons.
e: UAA, UAG, and UGA are terminator codons. Write terminator in the gap.

q: By convention, the genetic code is always interpreted in terms of the ____ codon rather than the nucleotide sequence of the DNA.
e: By convention, the genetic code is always interpreted in terms of the mRNA codon rather than the nucleotide sequence of the DNA. That missing piece is mRNA.

q: The genetic code is ____, meaning that more than one codon can code for the same amino acid.
e: The genetic code is redundant, meaning that more than one codon can code for the same amino acid. Write redundant in the gap.

q: There are only ____ codons that do not code for any amino acid.
e: There are only three codons that do not code for any amino acid. That missing piece is three.

q: These codons serve as "____" signals to end protein synthesis.
e: These codons serve as "stop" signals to end protein synthesis. The blank is stop.

q: The genetic code is ____, meaning that it reads as a series of three-letter codons without spaces, punctuation, or overlap.
e: The genetic code is continuous, meaning that it reads as a series of three-letter codons without spaces, punctuation, or overlap. Write continuous in the gap.

q: A ____ of one or two nucleotides in either direction can alter the codon groupings and result in an incorrect amino acid sequence.
e: A shift of one or two nucleotides in either direction can alter the codon groupings and result in an incorrect amino acid sequence. Write shift in the gap.

q: The genetic code is nearly ____, meaning almost all organisms build proteins with the same genetic code.
e: The genetic code is nearly universal, meaning almost all organisms build proteins with the same genetic code. That missing piece is universal.

q: The universality of the genetic code means that a codon in the fruit fly codes for the same amino acid as in a ____.
e: The universality of the genetic code means that a codon in the fruit fly codes for the same amino acid as in a human. That missing piece is human.

q: The two steps in protein synthesis are transcription and ____.
e: The two steps in protein synthesis are transcription and translation. That missing piece is translation.

q: In transcription, mRNA is synthesized based on the ____ template of a gene.
e: In transcription, mRNA is synthesized based on the DNA template of a gene. The blank is DNA.

q: The central dogma of molecular biology stated that genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to ____.
e: The central dogma of molecular biology stated that genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to protein. That missing piece is protein.

q: Transcription occurs in the ____ of the cell.
e: Transcription occurs in the nucleus of the cell. That missing piece is nucleus.

q: There are ____ defined stages in the transcription process; initiation, elongation, and termination.
e: There are three defined stages in the transcription process; initiation, elongation, and termination. That missing piece is three.

q: For each gene, only ____ strand of the double-stranded DNA molecule is transcribed.
e: For each gene, only one strand of the double-stranded DNA molecule is transcribed. Write one in the gap.

q: The transcribed strand is called the antisense strand or ____ strand.
e: The transcribed strand is called the antisense strand or template strand. Write template in the gap.

q: The other strand, which is not transcribed, is called the sense strand or ____ strand.
e: The other strand, which is not transcribed, is called the sense strand or coding strand. That missing piece is coding.

q: The sense strand has the same sequence as the product mRNA, with ____ instead of uracil.
e: The sense strand has the same sequence as the product mRNA, with thymine instead of uracil. That missing piece is thymine.

q: During the elongation phase, the ____ complex works its way along the DNA molecule, synthesizing a strand of mRNA.
e: During the elongation phase, the RNA polymerase complex works its way along the DNA molecule, synthesizing a strand of mRNA. That missing piece is RNA polymerase.

q: The RNA polymerase synthesizes a strand of mRNA that is complementary to the template strand of DNA in ____ direction.
e: The RNA polymerase synthesizes a strand of mRNA that is complementary to the template strand of DNA in 5' to 3' direction. That missing piece is 5' to 3'.

q: When the RNA polymerase complexes reach the ____ signal, they detach from the DNA strand.
e: When the RNA polymerase complexes reach the termination signal, they detach from the DNA strand. Write termination in the gap.

q: The newly synthesized mRNA is called precursor mRNA or ____.
e: The newly synthesized mRNA is called precursor mRNA or pre-mRNA. That missing piece is pre-mRNA.

q: Before moving out from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, modifications convert pre-mRNA to ____ mRNA.
e: Before moving out from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, modifications convert pre-mRNA to mature mRNA. Write mature in the gap.

q: Modification of mRNA includes addition of a 5' cap at ____ end.
e: Modification of mRNA includes addition of a 5' cap at 5' end. That missing piece is 5'.

q: Modification of mRNA includes addition of a 3' ____ tail at 3' end.
e: Modification of mRNA includes addition of a 3' poly-A tail at 3' end. Write poly-A in the gap.

q: Modification of mRNA includes removal of introns (non-coding regions) and the remaining ____ (coding regions) are joined.
e: Modification of mRNA includes removal of introns (non-coding regions) and the remaining exons (coding regions) are joined. The blank is exons.

q: The second stage of protein synthesis involves translation which occurs in the ____.
e: The second stage of protein synthesis involves translation which occurs in the cytoplasm. The blank is cytoplasm.

q: Translation is the conversion of a sequence of nucleotides into a sequence of ____ in the polypeptide chain.
e: Translation is the conversion of a sequence of nucleotides into a sequence of amino acid in the polypeptide chain. Write amino acid in the gap.

q: There are ____ subunits in the ribosome.
e: There are two subunits in the ribosome. That missing piece is two.

q: At the ____ subunit, mature mRNA is attached.
e: At the small subunit, mature mRNA is attached. Write small in the gap.

q: There are three binding sites for tRNA on the large subunit of ribosome: A site, ____ site and E site.
e: There are three binding sites for tRNA on the large subunit of ribosome: A site, P site and E site. Write P in the gap.

q: Each tRNA carries the specific amino acid at a time at its ____ stem.
e: Each tRNA carries the specific amino acid at a time at its acceptor stem. Write acceptor in the gap.

q: Opposite to the acceptor stem is the ____ which connects to the specific codon on the mRNA.
e: Opposite to the acceptor stem is the anticodon which connects to the specific codon on the mRNA. That missing piece is anticodon.

q: In the initiation phase, the small ribosomal sub-unit attaches to the mRNA near the ____ codon (AUG).
e: In the initiation phase, the small ribosomal sub-unit attaches to the mRNA near the start codon (AUG). The blank is start.

q: The first tRNA that binds to the codon is the initiator tRNA with its ____ anticodon.
e: The first tRNA that binds to the codon is the initiator tRNA with its UAC anticodon. That missing piece is UAC.

q: Then, a ____ ribosomal sub-unit joins to form the active ribosome.
e: Then, a large ribosomal sub-unit joins to form the active ribosome. That missing piece is large.

q: During elongation, a cycle of ____ steps is rapidly repeated.
e: During elongation, a cycle of four steps is rapidly repeated. Write four in the gap.

q: First, a tRNA with an attached polypeptide is in the P site, then, ____ bond is formed and tRNA carrying the next amino acid enters the A site.
e: First, a tRNA with an attached polypeptide is in the P site, then, peptide bond is formed and tRNA carrying the next amino acid enters the A site. Write peptide in the gap.

q: Next, the polypeptide chain is ____ to the amino acid of the tRNA in the A site.
e: Next, the polypeptide chain is transferred to the amino acid of the tRNA in the A site. That missing piece is transferred.

q: Last, the mRNA moves forward by ____ codon, and the polypeptide-bearing tRNA is now at the ribosome P site.
e: Last, the mRNA moves forward by one codon, and the polypeptide-bearing tRNA is now at the ribosome P site. The blank is one.

q: The ____ tRNA exits the ribosome.
e: The uncharged tRNA exits the ribosome. That missing piece is uncharged.

q: The termination phase begins when a ____ codon on the mRNA is reached.
e: The termination phase begins when a stop codon on the mRNA is reached. That missing piece is stop.

q: A protein, called a ____ factor, cleaves the polypeptide from the last tRNA.
e: A protein, called a release factor, cleaves the polypeptide from the last tRNA. Write release in the gap.

q: Scientists can now use ____ organisms (GMOs) to produce medications, to profile the DNA sequence of a cancerous tumour, and to treat genetic disorders.
e: Scientists can now use genetically modified organisms (GMOs) to produce medications, to profile the DNA sequence of a cancerous tumour, and to treat genetic disorders. That missing piece is genetically modified.

q: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the ____ material of an organism in a specific manner.
e: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the genetic material of an organism in a specific manner. Write genetic in the gap.

q: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms (____).
e: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms (GMOs). That missing piece is GMOs.

q: Transgenic describes an organism that is produced from the introduction of ____ DNA into its genome, providing it with a new phenotype.
e: Transgenic describes an organism that is produced from the introduction of foreign DNA into its genome, providing it with a new phenotype. Write foreign in the gap.

q: The ____ DNA techniques and methods of DNA analysis are integral to the production of GMOs.
e: The recombinant DNA techniques and methods of DNA analysis are integral to the production of GMOs. The blank is recombinant.

q: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene from one organism into the genome of another organism of ____ species.
e: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene from one organism into the genome of another organism of different species. Write different in the gap.

q: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a ____ is needed, which may be plasmid of bacteria, harmless virus, liposome or gene gun.
e: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a vector is needed, which may be plasmid of bacteria, harmless virus, liposome or gene gun. Write vector in the gap.

q: Rice is a ____ food in many parts of the world.
e: Rice is a staple food in many parts of the world. The blank is staple.

q: Vitamin A deficiency can cause ____.
e: Vitamin A deficiency can cause blindness. That missing piece is blindness.

q: Lack of vitamin A can cause an ____ deficiency syndrome, and this is a significant cause of mortality in some parts of the world.
e: Lack of vitamin A can cause an immune deficiency syndrome, and this is a significant cause of mortality in some parts of the world. That missing piece is immune.

q: The genes that give golden rice its ability to make beta-carotene in its endosperm come from daffodils and ____ bacteria.
e: The genes that give golden rice its ability to make beta-carotene in its endosperm come from daffodils and erwinia bacteria. Write erwinia in the gap.

q: As they infect the embryo, they transfer the genes that encode the instructions for making ____.
e: As they infect the embryo, they transfer the genes that encode the instructions for making beta-carotene. That missing piece is beta-carotene.

q: The transgenic rice plants must now be ____ with strains of rice that are grown locally.
e: The transgenic rice plants must now be crossed with strains of rice that are grown locally. Write crossed in the gap.

q: Further research showed that substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from ____ gave even higher quantities of carotene.
e: Further research showed that substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from maize gave even higher quantities of carotene. The blank is maize.

q: The genetically modified rice is called Golden Rice, because it contains a lot of the orange pigment beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin A when it is ____.
e: The genetically modified rice is called Golden Rice, because it contains a lot of the orange pigment beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin A when it is eaten. Write eaten in the gap.

q: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased crop yield, increased heat and ____ tolerance.
e: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased crop yield, increased heat and drought tolerance. The blank is drought.

q: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased resistance to a range of pests and ____.
e: Benefits of genetic engineering of crops include increased resistance to a range of pests and pathogens. The blank is pathogens.

q: Plants are also being engineered to produce ____ products.
e: Plants are also being engineered to produce medicinal products. Write medicinal in the gap.

q: Since the mid-1980s, products such as human growth hormone, clotting factors, and ____ have been produced in transgenic plants.
e: Since the mid-1980s, products such as human growth hormone, clotting factors, and antibodies have been produced in transgenic plants. Write antibodies in the gap.

q: One type of antibody made by ____ can deliver radioisotopes to tumour cells.
e: One type of antibody made by corn can deliver radioisotopes to tumour cells. The blank is corn.

q: Another antibody made by soybeans can be used to treat ____ herpes.
e: Another antibody made by soybeans can be used to treat genital herpes. The blank is genital.

q: The production of transgenic animals is a much more complex process than the production of transgenic plants, and not surprisingly, it is also highly ____.
e: The production of transgenic animals is a much more complex process than the production of transgenic plants, and not surprisingly, it is also highly controversial. The blank is controversial.

q: To produce transgenic animals, foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal ____ (egg) that is then fertilized.
e: To produce transgenic animals, foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal oocyte (egg) that is then fertilized. The blank is oocyte.

q: The fertilized egg is ____ in a host female and allowed to develop.
e: The fertilized egg is implanted in a host female and allowed to develop. Write implanted in the gap.

q: The resulting ____ are the transgenic form of the animal.
e: The resulting offspring are the transgenic form of the animal. Write offspring in the gap.

q: The procedure has been used to produce transgenic fish, pigs, cows, rabbits, and ____.
e: The procedure has been used to produce transgenic fish, pigs, cows, rabbits, and sheep. That missing piece is sheep.

q: Transgenic animals can be used to produce ____ products such as human proteins by using a recombinant plasmid vector.
e: Transgenic animals can be used to produce pharmaceutical products such as human proteins by using a recombinant plasmid vector. That missing piece is pharmaceutical.

q: The vector contains the gene for the growth protein as well as the ____ that directs the expression of the genes in mammary cells.
e: The vector contains the gene for the growth protein as well as the promoter that directs the expression of the genes in mammary cells. Write promoter in the gap.

q: The recombinant DNA is then ____ into an oocyte.
e: The recombinant DNA is then injected into an oocyte. The blank is injected.

q: The ____ of female transgenic offspring contains human growth protein.
e: The milk of female transgenic offspring contains human growth protein. The blank is milk.

q: Benefits of GM animals include greater ____ mass in animals used for meat.
e: Benefits of GM animals include greater muscle mass in animals used for meat. The blank is muscle.

q: GM animals can be used for manufacture of human proteins, such as antibodies, blood ____ factors.
e: GM animals can be used for manufacture of human proteins, such as antibodies, blood clotting factors. The blank is clotting.

q: GM animals allow production of organs for transplantation, also known as ____.
e: GM animals allow production of organs for transplantation, also known as xero-transplantation. That missing piece is xero-transplantation.
